verdict.name: Ukrainian Catholic University (Faculty of Health Sciences; no medical faculty found)
corrections: NEW AUTHORITY LEAD (the record said only a loda.gov.ua news item was found). Search 2 returned universities.studyinukraine.gov.ua/en/minedu/university/172/, titled 'Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine', and studyinukraine.gov.ua/study-in-ukraine/universities/?lang=3. Both are on the government Study in Ukraine portal. According to the summary, 'a Ukrainian government study portal' lists UCU's degrees. Undergraduate: Theology, History, Culture Studies, Philology, Social Pedagogy, Psychology, Sociology, Computer Science. Graduate: Theology, History, Social Pedagogy, Journalism, Media Communications, Public Administration, Clinical Psychology (CBT), Clinical Psychology (Psychodynamic Therapy), Data Science, Human Rights, Physical Therapy, Ergotherapy. The portal also says UCU offers language training in four languages. The summary did not say which of the two portal URLs carried this text; I matched it to /university/172/ only by inference. The page was not opened and is undated, and the list may be old: it has no Faculty of Law and no physical therapy bachelor's. It is a portal profile, not EDEBO registration or licence evidence, and it lists no medical, dental, pharmacy or nursing programme.

SECOND INDEPENDENT DOMAIN SOURCE: an Erasmus+ information sheet from Universidad Autonoma de Madrid (third-party, https://www.uam.es/uam/media/doc/1606871221478/uc-ukranian-university.pdf) gives the UCU international office email as international@ucu.edu.ua. This matches the ucu.edu.ua official pages and the Wikipedia lead already in the record. The sheet is aimed at exchange partners, not full-degree applicants.

UCU's own subdomains appeared in search 3: strategy.ucu.edu.ua/en/etapy/ (a strategy timeline listing the Health Sciences, Social Sciences and Applied Sciences faculties) and law.ucu.edu.ua/en/?p=14 ('ABOUT THE LAW Faculty'). Both are official, undated, and count as one publisher family with ucu.edu.ua.

FACULTY STRUCTURE UPDATE: ugcc.ua is the Ukrainian Greek Catholic Church's site. It is affiliated with UCU but on a separate domain. A September 2025 article there says a renovated UCU building on Sventsitskoho Street in Lviv was consecrated, and that it houses the Faculty of Social Sciences, the Faculty of Health Sciences and a newly created Faculty of Law with a Legal Clinic. The record's unattributed, undated list of 'six degree-granting faculties' is therefore probably out of date.

DATED OPERATING LEAD: according to the summary, the same ugcc.ua article (September 2025) says more than 1,100 students will study in the renovated Lviv building. This adds to the hromada.us report dated 2026-08-17. Neither describes how teaching is delivered.

'Private' status now has third-party corroboration: the search 3 summary calls UCU a private university in Lviv affiliated with the Ukrainian Catholic Church, which grew out of the Lviv Theological Academy (the Greek Catholic Theological Academy founded in 1928, resumed in the 1990s). The summary did not say which result this came from (encyclopediaofukraine.com, uni2study.com or abitly.org). Ownership form is still not verified in EDEBO.

MISLABELLING IN A SEARCH SUMMARY: search 2 called the hromada.us physical-therapy article 'a UCU page'. It is third-party (hromada.us). The record already labels it correctly as third-party. No official ucu.edu.ua page on the new physical therapy bachelor's turned up.

DATE INCONSISTENCY TO NOTE: the search 2 summary calls the uacrisis.org piece a 2016 press release announcing two-year master's programmes. hromada.us (2026) says UCU has trained specialists through master's programmes in occupational and physical therapy 'since 2018'. The record says rehabilitation programmes 'began in 2016'. That should read 'announced in 2016 (uacrisis); training since 2018 (hromada.us)' until an official source confirms.

EDEBO/LICENCE SEARCH (search 1, in Ukrainian, on specialty 227 Physical Therapy and licence) found no UCU licence record. UCU appeared only in a Uzhhorod National University programme document, as the workplace of one team member. This is not evidence of a UCU 227 licence or programme. The absence of a result is an access/search limitation, not evidence that no licence exists. A mon.gov.ua licensing-protocol PDF (Prot 252, 11.10.2022) also appeared, but nothing in the result tied it to UCU.
refutedLeads: Criterion 3 fails. No official-domain result shows a medical, dental, pharmacy or nursing programme open to foreign applicants. The only official page on foreign students (ucu.edu.ua/?p=74383, undated) names Data Science (Faculty of Applied Sciences) as the English-taught degree track. It says the psychology and social work bachelor's programmes require Ukrainian. Physical Therapy and Ergotherapy are rehabilitation/allied-health programmes, not medicine, dentistry, pharmacy or nursing. No result, official or third-party, says they are taught in English or open to foreigners.

The loda.gov.ua item about a UCU medical clinic (Panasa Myrnoho 24a) is a news item about a rehabilitation clinic. It is not a registry listing and not evidence of any medical education programme or licence.

The claim that the master's programmes were 'designed to meet WCPT/WFOT requirements' (uacrisis.org, third-party, reported as a 2016 press release) is a design claim. It is not NAQA accreditation, international accreditation or destination-country recognition.
The 'six degree-granting faculties' list in the record is unattributed and undated. A September 2025 ugcc.ua report of a newly created Faculty of Law contradicts it as a current list.
The UCU mention in the Uzhhorod National University 227 programme document is only a team member's workplace. It does not show a UCU programme or licence in specialty 227.
verdict.reason: Criterion 1 holds at lead level. The name 'Ukrainian Catholic University' and the domain ucu.edu.ua agree across the university's own pages and subdomains (ucu.edu.ua, strategy., law., er., international@) and independent third parties (the UAM Erasmus sheet giving international@ucu.edu.ua, and Wikipedia per the record). EDEBO was not checked. Criterion 2 holds as a lead only. The government Study in Ukraine portal (universities.studyinukraine.gov.ua/en/minedu/university/172/) appeared, and the summary says the portal lists UCU degrees, including graduate Physical Therapy and Ergotherapy. Matching that text to the exact URL is my inference. The page was not opened, the list looks dated, and it is not registration or licence evidence. Criterion 3 fails. No official-domain result shows a medical, dental, pharmacy or nursing programme open to foreigners. UCU's health unit offers rehabilitation (physical therapy, ergotherapy), psychology and social work. The undated official foreign-student page names only Data Science as an English degree track and says psychology and social work need Ukrainian. No 222 Medicine programme appeared anywhere, and that absence is a search limitation, not proof. Criterion 4: no relocation, occupation, closure, merger or licence-withdrawal lead was found. Lviv-based activity is reported in dated third-party sources from September 2025 (ugcc.ua, building consecration, 1,100+ students) and August 2026 (hromada.us, new physical therapy bachelor's). State licence scope remains unverified in EDEBO, but that is a verification gap, not an open status question. Because criterion 3 fails, previewEligible is false. The recommendation stays defer, not reject: the site's MD-focused audience is out of scope, but official pages and registries could not be opened. Revisit only if official ucu.edu.ua or international.ucu.edu.ua pages, or EDEBO and NAQA records, show a regulated health programme open to foreign applicants.

Most evidence comes from third-party aggregators (vstup.osvita.ua, education.ua, osvita.ua). vstup.osvita.ua draws on admissions data but is not a government domain, so I recorded it as third-party.

What this angle could not cover:
(1) No full list of institutions offering bachelor-level Nursing (specialty 223 / I5) came back. The vstup.osvita.ua specialty search pages (spec/9-530-4/..., spec/1-40-1/..., spec/9-40-2/...) appeared in results but I did not open them. One page reported 76 specialties for 2026, but the institutions on it were not listed.
(2) I did not confirm a first-cycle bachelor Nursing offer for Cherkasy Medical Academy, Rivne Medical Academy or Kharkiv National Medical University. For Volyn Medical Institute and Zhytomyr Medical Institute, the Nursing offers found show a 1 year 9 month duration and a Bachelor admission basis, so they may be master's programmes.
(3) I found no communal medical academy or institute of a regional council in Khmelnytskyi, Vinnytsia, Kherson or other oblasts beyond those listed. This is a search limitation, not evidence that none exist.
(4) Colleges: the Kherson and Nikopol colleges appear only because MON licence documents mention bachelor-level training. I left out Kremenchuk Medical Professional College named after V.I. Lytvynenko and the Lviv Franko medical professional college (MON document KZFPO...Franka) because nothing showed bachelor-degree provision.
(5) I did not search for Nursing bachelor provision at most of the other known universities, so those absences mean nothing.
(6) I checked no accreditation (NAQA), licence status, recognition or current teaching location, and found no dated relocation statements.
(7) The MON draft higher-education standards for I5 Nursing (bachelor, master, PhD) were posted for public consultation on 21 July 2026 at mon.gov.ua. They are drafts, not institution evidence.

sweeps.coverageNote:
I used all 6 WebSearch calls (standard mode, no WebFetch). Four were restricted to universities.studyinukraine.gov.ua. The search tool gives back titles, URLs and a model-written summary, not the raw pages, so every programme, fee and date above is a lead from undated portal pages and has not been verified. The portal's own specialty filter (Medicine 222, Dentistry 221, General Medicine 7.1201001, etc.) and its full directory could not be listed. This sweep is therefore a sample of indexed portal pages, not a complete list of medical-programme institutions on the portal.

Gaps and limits:
(1) Portal IDs 14, 24 and 92 came back from one search. Its summary described an Ivano-Frankivsk medical university, a private Dnipro medical institute and a Zhytomyr nursing institution, but never said which ID was which. The Dnipro and Zhytomyr entries stay unmatched, and the IFNMU match rests on city plus programme profile.
(2) Linking ID 82 to Poltava State Medical University is my inference from the summary.
(3) Some institutions appeared on the portal without any medical programme shown, so I did not include them: Ivan Franko National University of Lviv (101, preparatory school only), Kyiv International University (117, title only), Lviv Polytechnic (166), NTU 'KhPI' (83), Vasyl' Stus Donetsk National University (79) and Odessa National Maritime University (39).
(4) Two more leads fell outside this angle and were not used: Sumy State University (Careers360 third-party fee range, not medicine-specific) and an iie.karazin.ua PDF (official Karazin domain, content not described).
(5) I found nothing from the Ukrainian State Centre for International Education that lists institutions. The only UCIE-related result was aggregate statistics on the portal (studyinukraine.gov.ua/?p=6548, as summarised): Medicine about 32%, Medical Care about 7.7%, Dentistry about 6% and Pharmacy about 3.1% of foreign students' popular choices.
(6) The portal's general claims about medicine study in Ukraine (average cost EUR 1,500-5,000 per year; two versions of the page disagree on on-campus-only versus online delivery) are not tied to any institution, so they are not used.
(7) Many known institutions did not surface in these 6 searches. That is a search-coverage limit, not evidence of absence. They include Dnipro State Medical University, Uzhhorod NU, Sumy SU, Karazin, the private Kyiv/Odesa/Lviv institutions, Luhansk SMU (Rivne) and Cherkasy Medical Academy.
(8) None of the results said anything about accreditation, recognition, location, relocation or teaching format, and none of that is implied here. A portal listing is not proof of licence, NAQA accreditation or foreign recognition.

sweeps.coverageNote:
I used 6 standard searches and no WebFetch. The search tool gave summaries, not full pages, so several figures could not be tied to one exact URL in the result set. Those entries say so, and each attribution needs checking before use. Agency lists in 2025-2026 mostly repeat the large state medical universities, all of which are already known. The only private or 'international' institutions that came up with any content were Kyiv Medical University (formerly UAFM) and Kharkiv International Medical University. The only institution not on the known list was Crimea State Medical University (Simferopol, occupied Crimea). The agency found markets it as 'MBBS in Russia', not Ukraine, so it is a disambiguation and occupied-territory flag, not a confirmed case of 'marketed as Ukrainian'.

Conflicts between sources:
- Bogomolets fees: about USD 4,500 (admitkard) against USD 2,500-4,500 (Careers360).
- Odesa National Medical University fees: about USD 4,700 (admitkard) against USD 8,000 (Careers360 listing), plus a probable data error of about INR 7.84K.
- Crimea: the agency claims 'NMC-recognized', while an older Indian parliamentary document says MCI does not recognise Russian degrees.
- Several 'NMC-approved' tables are only consultancy claims.

Searched for but no usable result in this angle: Odesa International Medical University, International European University, Black Sea National University (Mykolaiv), Bohdan Khmelnytsky Cherkasy, V. N. Karazin Kharkiv National University, Kherson and Mariupol medical faculties, and agency names or commissions. Luhansk and Donetsk appeared only as regions in the older Indian parliamentary document, not as institutions with marketing content, so I did not record them.

Context leads, not tied to any one institution:
- The Study in Ukraine portal (studyinukraine.gov.ua/program_cat/study-mbbs-in-ukraine/) reportedly says MBBS programmes in Ukraine are delivered only on campus.
- Interfax (2025) reports 816,000 applications for medicine during the 2025 admission campaign.

Not enumerated:
- The full catalogues of large aggregators, such as selectyouruniversity, careers360 and mbbsadmissionabroad. Their full tables were not visible, and they may list more private institutions.
- Smaller agency sites and non-Indian agencies, such as those aimed at Nigeria, Egypt, Morocco or Central Asia.
- Any official confirmation of names, licences, NAQA accreditation, recognition, fees, intakes or current operating location. None of these were checked, so every entry remains a lead only.

sweeps.coverageNote: Six standard WebSearch queries; no WebFetch, and no official or government page was opened. Every item is a lead taken from search summaries and titles, not a verified fact. CANNOT ENUMERATE: (1) The full list of displaced institutions with health programmes. The Ombudsman (ombudsman.gov.ua, 08/06/2022, citing MON) reports 32 higher education institutions, 42 colleges and 64 branches evacuated from occupied Donetsk, Luhansk, Kherson and Zaporizhzhia oblasts. Atlantic Council reports 18 universities displaced in 2014 (9 Donetsk, 8 Luhansk, 1 Crimea), and its article title calls Taurida the only displaced Crimean university, which suggests the Crimean medical university did not relocate as a Ukrainian institution (unconfirmed). Neither source names the medical or health institutions, and the 2025 Finikov et al. relocation map was seen only as an abstract. (2) Relocated medical colleges. Only the Bakhmut college surfaced. Nothing was found on Donetsk Regional Medical College, or on medical colleges from Luhansk/Sievierodonetsk/Lysychansk, Mariupol, Kherson, Melitopol, Berdiansk or Kramatorsk, though they likely exist. (3) Russian-run institutions in occupied Zaporizhzhia and Kherson oblasts. Reports say a Russian-installed 'Melitopol State University' was built from the seized Melitopol State Pedagogical University and Tavria State Agrotechnological University (stopfake.org; mediacenter.org.ua, June 2022; radiosvoboda.org). No medical or health faculty was found, so it is NOT listed as a health institution. Nothing found for Kherson, Mariupol, Luhansk medical colleges or a Sevastopol State University medical unit. (4) Luhansk State Medical University named after St. Luke (occupied Luhansk), already known, did not appear in these searches. Kherson State University and Zaporizhzhia institutions also did not appear for this angle. (5) Allied-health programmes (e.g. physical therapy) at displaced non-medical universities such as Luhansk Taras Shevchenko NU, Donetsk NU (Vasyl Stus), Mariupol SU and Berdiansk SPU were not searched. Not checked anywhere: EDEBO entries, licences, NAQA accreditation, Ukrainian government statements on diploma non-recognition for the Crimean and Donetsk occupation-side institutions, and current teaching locations or formats. The dnrsovet.gov.ru item is from an occupation authority and is classed as third-party, not government.
